newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Jiangling sets up venture with Ford unit.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiangling sets up venture with Ford unit.

text.p: China's Jiangling Motors Corp Ltd will set up a joint venture with Lear Corp, a unit of Ford Motor Co, to make car and light-truck interior components, the Securities Times reported on Thursday.
The newspaper, based in Shenzhen, China, said an agreement on the project was signed on Wednesday in Nanchang, capital of Jiangxi province.

The venture, which requires a total investment of US$30 million, has a registered capital of US$14.60 million, with Jiangling and Lear each holding a 50-percent stake. Jiangling will contribute assets and Lear will provide cash, it said.

The Nanchang-based Lear Interior Decoration System Co Ltd will specialise in such products as seats and air-conditioners for cars and light trucks, and will be operational in September of 1997, the newspaper said.
The venture's products will be bought mainly by Jiangling Motors, with the rest to be exported, it said.

Xiong Zhongping, a spokesman for Jiangling, last month told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that Jiangling would soon establish a "sister relationship" with Cleveland Engine & Casting Plants, also a subsidiary of Ford.

Xiong said Cleveland would provide training courses for Jiangling's staff in management and production technology. Cleveland and Jiangling would also co-operate in engine manufacturing, he said without giving details. Jiangling's co-operation with Ford dates to 1995, when Ford paid about US$40 million to purchase 80 percent of Jiangling's 174 million class B shares.

At that time, Jiangling had total share capital of 693.214 million shares, including 353.24 million state shares, 174 million B shares, 117.6 million A shares and 48.374 million shares held by institutions.

Xiong said Jiangling's net profits this year would rise sharply from the previous year. He said Jiangling had posted strong third-quarter results, with net profits in September hitting about nine million yuan.
He did not give a profit figure for July-September, but said Jiangling's fourth-quarter results would be even stronger.
